entries_new.name: Virginia Company
entries_new.founder: Investors in London, chartered by the English king
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave a joint-stock company the right to settle and govern a stretch of the North American coast.
entries_new.story: The Virginia Company was an English trading company that received a royal charter on 10 April 1606 to colonise the east coast of North America, a stretch named Virginia that ran from present-day Maine to the Carolinas. Its shareholders were Londoners. A separate company of Plymouth gentlemen was chartered at the same time. After a 1622 attack by Indigenous people killed many colonists, the company failed, and on 24 May 1624 the king dissolved it and made Virginia a royal colony. Colonists kept a lower house, the House of Burgesses.

entries_new.name: Council for New England
entries_new.founder: Sir Ferdinando Gorges was a key promoter
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave a company the right to grant and settle land across a defined band of North America.
entries_new.story: The Council for New England was an English joint stock company that received a royal charter in November 1620 with the aim of extending the king's realm in North America through settlements. Its charter covered land between the 40th and 48th parallels, which the text describes as the part of the Virginia Colony north of the 40th parallel. It was disbanded in 1635, with no apparent change in land titles. It provided for the Plymouth Colony, the Province of New Hampshire, the Massachusetts Bay Colony, the New Haven Colony and the Province of Maine.

entries_new.name: Somers Isles Company
entries_new.stopped_by: Dissolved in 1684; the Crown took over
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave a company the islands to run as a commercial venture.
entries_new.story: The Somers Isles Company was formed in 1615 to run Bermuda, also called the Somers Isles, as a commercial venture. The islands had been settled by accident in 1609, when the Virginia Company's flagship Sea Venture was wrecked on the reefs. The new company held a royal charter for Bermuda until 1684, when it was dissolved and the Crown took over the administration, making Bermuda a royal colony.

entries_new.name: Providence Island Company
entries_new.founder: Robert Rich, 2nd Earl of Warwick, and Puritan investors
entries_new.mechanism: A charter gave a group of investors a Caribbean island to settle and use as a privateering base.
entries_new.story: The Providence Island Company was an English company founded in 1629 by Puritan investors, among them Robert Rich, 2nd Earl of Warwick, to settle Providence Island, now part of Colombia's San Andrés y Providencia Department. Settlers ran plantations. The colonies also served as a base for privateers (ship owners licensed to attack an enemy's shipping) working against Spanish ships and settlements, with one fifth of plunder owed to the company. A patent was granted on 4 December 1630. The Spanish and Portuguese destroyed the colonies in 1641.

entries_new.name: Massachusetts Bay Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter let a company's investors move to America and govern the colony themselves.
entries_new.story: The Massachusetts Bay Company was a joint-stock company set up by English royal charter that founded the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1628, around Salem and Boston. The colony's nominal territory covered much of central New England. About 20,000 people migrated there in the 1630s, and governors were chosen by an electorate limited to freemen admitted to the local church. The colony took part in the Pequot War (1636 to 1638) and King Philip's War (1675 to 1678). In 1691 its territory was reorganised as the Province of Massachusetts Bay.

entries_new.name: Dutch West India Company
entries_new.mechanism: A state charter gave a company a trade monopoly and the right to hold and run overseas colonies.
entries_new.story: The Dutch West India Company was chartered on 3 June 1621 by the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands, with a trade monopoly across West Africa and the Americas and jurisdiction over Dutch participation in the Atlantic slave trade, Brazil, the Caribbean and North America. It founded New Netherland, which included New Amsterdam on Manhattan, and from 1624 to 1654 held part of northeast Brazil before being driven out. The first company dissolved in 1674 over debts. A second charter in 1675 lasted until 1792.

entries_new.name: Society of Berbice
entries_new.mechanism: Colony owners pooled capital into a share-issuing company that governed the colony.
entries_new.story: The Society of Berbice was founded on 24 October 1720 by five owners of the colony of Berbice, in present-day Guyana, who had bought it from the French in 1714. It was a public company listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange and raised capital for the colony, which at one point held 12 society plantations beside 93 private plantations on the Berbice River. A slave uprising under Coffy in February 1763 caused plantation losses and financial trouble. Berbice was ceded to Britain, the last plantations were sold in November 1818, and the offices closed in 1821.

entries_new.name: Society of Suriname
entries_new.mechanism: Three shareholders jointly ran a colony under a charter from the Dutch state.
entries_new.story: The Society of Suriname was a Dutch private company set up on 21 May 1683 to profit from the management and defence of the Dutch colony of Suriname. It had three equal participants: the city of Amsterdam, the Van Aerssen van Sommelsdijck family and the Dutch West India Company. All Dutch citizens could trade with Suriname, and planters were consulted in a Council of Police, a feature the text calls unique among the Guyana colonies. The Batavian Republic nationalised the Society in November 1795.

entries_new.name: Danish East India Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter plus a treaty with a local ruler gave a company a fortified trading town.
entries_new.story: The Danish East India Company refers to two Danish-Norwegian chartered companies, the first from 1616 to 1650 and the second from 1670 to 1729. Under a treaty of 19 November 1620 the ruler of Tanjore, Raghunatha Nayak, gave the Danes the town of Tranquebar in India, where they built Dansborg. The first company lost all acquisitions except Tranquebar. Dansborg was ceded to the second company in 1670. The second company was dissolved in 1729 and re-founded in 1730 as the Asiatic Company.

entries_new.name: Danish West India Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave a company the right to settle and govern Caribbean islands.
entries_new.story: The Danish West India Company, also called the West India-Guinea Company, was a Dano-Norwegian chartered company formally chartered by King Christian V on 11 March 1671. The Danes settled St Thomas in 1668, bought St John in 1718 and St Croix from the French in 1733. It also traded on the Danish Gold Coast, and an estimated 120,000 enslaved Africans were carried on its ships. The company governed the colonies until 1754, when the Danish government's Chamber of Revenues took control.

entries_new.name: Sierra Leone Company
entries_new.founder: Granville Sharp, Henry Thornton, Thomas Clarkson and others
entries_new.mechanism: An Act of Parliament, not a royal charter, incorporated a company to run a settlement.
entries_new.story: The Sierra Leone Company was the body that founded the second British colony in Africa on 11 March 1792. It was set up under the Sierra Leone Company Act 1791 after attempts to win a royal charter failed. In 1792 John Clarkson led over 1,100 Black settlers from Halifax, Nova Scotia, most of them former slaves of the American colonies freed by the British, to found Freetown. Slave-trade merchants and West India planters petitioned against the bill, which passed Parliament 87 votes to 9.

entries_new.name: Van Diemen's Land Company
entries_new.challenge: Peerapper people, who were killed or removed
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter and an Act of Parliament gave a company a large land grant to farm.
entries_new.story: The Van Diemen's Land Company is a farming company in Tasmania, founded in 1825 with a royal charter and granted 250,000 acres in the north-west of the island in 1826. By 1828 the grant was increased to 350,000 acres in several large blocks. Its manager Edward Curr is quoted as saying the land could only be held by exterminating or expelling the Peerapper people. The text states that company employees carried out massacres, including at Cape Grim, and that by 1835 the Peerapper were gone from the region. Parts of the land were sold in 2016 and 2021.

entries_new.name: Canada Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter let a company buy and resell the unsettled lands of a colony.
entries_new.story: The Canada Company was a British land company incorporated by royal charter on 19 August 1826. In 1827 it bought the undeveloped clergy and Crown reserves of Upper Canada for 341,000 pounds. Its main project was the Huron Tract, which it surveyed, divided into lots, and advertised to buyers in Europe, laying out Goderich on Lake Huron as the centre. The settlement dispossessed the Mississauga people of their ancestral lands. John Galt, the first superintendent, founded Guelph. The company voted to wind up on 12 August 1953 and was dissolved on 18 December 1953.

entries_new.name: South Australian Company
entries_new.mechanism: A private firm met the land-purchase condition of a colonisation Act, which allowed settlement to start.
entries_new.story: The South Australian Company was formed in London on 9 October 1835 after the 1834 Act created the Province of South Australia. It was a commercial firm unconnected to the government or the Colonisation Commission, led by George Fife Angas, and it bought unsold land to the level the Act required so emigration could start. In 1836 four ships settled Kingscote on Kangaroo Island, and the company then moved to the mainland, providing basic infrastructure and selling or leasing land to immigrants. It was wound up on 17 March 1949.

entries_new.name: Eastern Archipelago Company
entries_new.recognition: British Crown; Sultan of Brunei rights
entries_new.mechanism: Coal rights obtained from a Bornean sultan were turned into a royal charter for land and mining on an island.
entries_new.story: The Eastern Archipelago Company was incorporated by British royal charter in 1847 and was active on the island of Labuan, off the coast of Borneo, until it was dissolved in 1858. Henry Wise, a former East India Company maritime officer, had acquired the coal rights from James Brooke, the White Rajah of Sarawak, who had obtained them from the Sultan of Brunei. The charter let the company buy, hold, settle and sell land on Labuan and nearby, mine coal and trade with the island's inhabitants.

entries_new.name: German New Guinea Company
entries_new.mechanism: An imperial charter delegated rule of a protectorate to a private company.
entries_new.story: The German New Guinea Company was founded in Berlin in 1884 by Adolph von Hansemann and a syndicate of bankers to colonise and exploit north-eastern New Guinea and nearby islands. Chancellor Bismarck ordered a protectorate on 19 August of that year. For the first fifteen years the colony was run under imperial charters by the private company. From 1899 to 1914 the German government administered German New Guinea through a governor. The government's priority was rapid economic development based on a German-controlled plantation economy.

entries_new.name: German East Africa Company
entries_new.founder: Carl Peters, among its principal founders
entries_new.recognition: German Empire; Sultan of Zanzibar lease
entries_new.mechanism: A lease from a sultan plus a German charter gave a company the right to administer a coastal strip.
entries_new.story: The German East Africa Company originated in 1884 as the Society for German Colonisation. In April 1885 it leased the coastal strip opposite Zanzibar from Sultan Khalifa bin Said for 50 years. Its attempt to take over administration provoked a general revolt along the coast of what is now Tanzania. The company held Dar es Salaam and Bagamoyo only with help from the German navy, and in 1889 asked the government to put the rebellion down. In 1891 it sold out to the German government, which then ruled German East Africa directly.

entries_new.name: German West African Company
entries_new.mechanism: A charter gave a company commercial rights in two protectorates without governing powers.
entries_new.story: The German West African Company was a German chartered company founded in 1885 with headquarters in Hamburg. It exploited the two German protectorates of Togo and Cameroon but, unlike its counterpart in German East Africa, did not actually govern them. After years of little profit, the German Empire absorbed the company on 13 November 1903.

entries_new.name: Mozambique Company
entries_new.mechanism: A Portuguese royal charter handed tax collection, labour and land rights over two provinces to a company.
entries_new.story: The Mozambique Company held a 50-year concession over the lands of what are now Manica and Sofala provinces in central Mozambique. It was set up on 11 February 1891 with capital from German, British and South African financiers. It had the exclusive right to collect taxes, could grant sub-concessions, and used forced labour (the chibalo system). Resistance to forced labour led to rebellions against it in 1902 and 1917. Under the Salazar regime, Portugal did not renew the concession, and on 18 July 1942 the territory passed to the colonial administration.

entries_new.name: Niassa Company
entries_new.mechanism: A Portuguese royal charter gave a company rule and taxation of two northern provinces.
entries_new.story: The Niassa Company, also called the Nyassa Chartered Company, held a concession from 1891 to 1929 over the current Cabo Delgado and Niassa provinces of Mozambique, more than 160,000 square kilometres between the Ruvuma and Lúrio rivers. The Portuguese government issued the formal charter in March 1893. Its founder's syndicate failed to raise capital, so French and British investors bought the concession and moved headquarters to London. The company relied on a hut tax, raised from 2 escudos in 1921 to 85 in 1929. The concession ended on 27 October 1929, with the company owing over a million pounds.

entries_new.name: Russian-American Company
entries_new.challenge: Britain and the United States disputed its southern border
entries_new.mechanism: An imperial decree gave one company a monopoly and rule over Russian America.
entries_new.story: The Russian-American Company was a state-sponsored chartered company created by Emperor Paul's decree of 1799 to settle Russian America, trade with Indigenous people and expand colonisation. Its monopoly originally ran south to 55 degrees North, later claimed to 51 degrees North, a border challenged by Britain and the United States and settled in the treaties of 1824 and 1825. Alexander Baranov founded Pavlovskaya and New Archangel (now Sitka). Aleut and Alutiiq men were forcibly conscripted to work for it. Alaska was sold to the United States in 1867.

entries_new.name: Company of Scotland (Darien scheme)
entries_new.founder: William Paterson led the Darien scheme
entries_new.mechanism: An act of the Scottish Parliament gave a company monopoly rights and sovereign powers overseas.
entries_new.story: The Company of Scotland Trading to Africa and the Indies, also called the Scottish Darien Company, was created by an act of the Parliament of Scotland in 1695, with a monopoly of Scottish trade to India, Africa and the Americas, sovereign rights and 21 years of tax exemption. In July 1698 it sent five ships and 1,200 colonists to Darien on the Isthmus of Panama. The settlement was poorly supplied and abandoned; a second expedition was besieged by Spain, and more than a thousand died of hunger and disease. The venture drained an estimated quarter of Scotland's liquid assets and helped lead to the Act of Union 1707.

entries_new.name: Company of One Hundred Associates
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave investors a fur-trade monopoly in return for settling a colony.
entries_new.story: The Company of One Hundred Associates, formally the Company of New France, was chartered in 1627 under Cardinal Richelieu to run the fur trade and to administer and expand French colonies in North America, centred on the Saint Lawrence valley. In return it was to settle French Catholics there. Each of 100 investors put in 3,000 livres. Samuel de Champlain was its commander in New France from 1629 to 1635. War with England and conflict with the Iroquois hurt it. In 1663 Louis XIV dissolved the company and made New France a province.

entries_new.name: Government of the Autonomous Republic of Abkhazia (in exile)
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed provincial government keeps its offices in the national capital to assert a continuing claim to its territory.
entries_new.story: This is a Georgian provincial government for Abkhazia, an autonomous republic within Georgia, led by Ruslan Abashidze. It has been based in Tbilisi since 1993, because Abkhaz separatists control the territory, which functions as a de facto independent state. It is listed as a deposed government of a subnational territory: it claims authority over an area that another administration holds.

entries_new.name: Ukrainian governments of Crimea and Sevastopol (in exile)
entries_new.mechanism: Regional governments relocated to continue to claim their territory after annexation.
entries_new.story: After Russia annexed Crimea in March 2014, following a status referendum that is disputed, the Ukrainian governments of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the City of Sevastopol moved to nearby Kherson. They stayed there until the 2022 Russian invasion and the occupation of Kherson Oblast. They now operate remotely within Ukraine. The Wikipedia list places them among deposed governments of subnational territories: bodies that claim authority over land they no longer control.

entries_new.name: Luhansk Oblast administration (in exile)
entries_new.mechanism: A regional administration continues to operate away from its seized territory.
entries_new.story: The Ukrainian administration of Luhansk Oblast is listed as a government in exile from 2022. Russian-backed separatists in the Luhansk People's Republic seized about 30 percent of the oblast in 2014, and the rest was taken in 2022 during the Russian invasion. Russia annexed the area on 30 September 2022. The oblast administration now operates remotely in Ukraine, although Ukraine regained a small slice of territory near Kharkiv Oblast in the 2022 counteroffensive.

entries_new.name: Committee for the Five Northern Korean Provinces
entries_new.mechanism: A body inside one state names itself the administration of provinces held by another state.
entries_new.story: Based in Seoul, the Committee for the Five Northern Korean Provinces is the South Korean government's provisional administration for five provinces that became part of North Korea at the end of the Second World War and the division of Korea. The five are North Hamgyeong, South Hamgyeong, Hwanghae, North Pyongan and South Pyongan. It was set up in 1949 and is listed among alternative governments in exile.

entries_new.name: National Council of Resistance of Iran
entries_new.mechanism: An opposition coalition abroad presents itself as a government-in-waiting.
entries_new.story: The National Council of Resistance of Iran, founded in 1981, is a political umbrella coalition of Iranian opposition organisations, of which the largest is the People's Mujahedin of Iran. Led by Maryam and Massoud Rajavi and based in Paris, it aims to establish a Democratic Republic of Iran to replace religious rule in Iran. The Wikipedia list places it among alternative governments in exile of current states. The Iranian government opposes it.

entries_new.name: Iran National Council
entries_new.mechanism: An opposition coalition abroad presents itself as an alternative to the ruling government.
entries_new.story: The Iran National Council is a political umbrella coalition of Iranian opposition groups, led by Prince Reza Pahlavi and based in Potomac, Maryland. It was formed in 2013 and is listed among alternative governments in exile of current states, meaning a body that has set itself up abroad and seeks to become the governing authority at home.

entries_new.name: Third Republic of Vietnam (Provisional National Government)
entries_new.mechanism: Exiles abroad proclaimed a government for the country they had left.
entries_new.story: The Third Republic of Vietnam, earlier named the Provisional National Government of Vietnam, was formed in Orange County, California, by former soldiers and refugees from South Vietnam. The Wikipedia list gives 1990 as the start and 1991 for its proclamation. Vietnam declared it a terrorist organisation. It is listed among alternative governments in exile of current states, which claim to speak for a country governed by someone else.

entries_new.name: Third Republic of Equatorial Guinea (Severo Moto)
entries_new.challenge: Government of Equatorial Guinea under Obiang
entries_new.mechanism: An exiled politician proclaimed himself president of a government meant to replace the ruling one.
entries_new.story: In 2003 a group proclaimed Severo Moto as president of Equatorial Guinea in exile, aiming to found a Third Republic and overthrow Teodoro Obiang's government. It was based in Madrid. The Wikipedia list places it among alternative governments in exile of current states.

entries_new.name: Ukraine Salvation Committee
entries_new.mechanism: Ministers who fled after a change of government formed a body claiming to be the lawful one.
entries_new.story: After the Revolution of Dignity in Ukraine, Prime Minister Mykola Azarov and pro-Russian, pro-Yanukovych members of the Second Azarov government fled to Russia and set up a government in exile. It was proclaimed in 2015 and aimed to restore the Azarov government. The Wikipedia list places it among alternative governments in exile of current states.

entries_new.name: Provisional Government of Free Joseon
entries_new.mechanism: A group abroad proclaims a provisional government for a state it does not control.
entries_new.story: The Provisional Government of Free Joseon is based in Seoul and claims North Korea as its territory. It is listed among alternative governments in exile, formed in 2017. The Wikipedia list notes it for protecting the family of Kim Jong-nam, including Kim Han-sol, after Kim Jong-nam was assassinated in Malaysia.

entries_new.name: Coordination Council for the Transfer of Power (Belarus)
entries_new.mechanism: An opposition leader abroad heads a council claiming a mandate from a disputed election.
entries_new.story: The Coordination Council opposes Alexander Lukashenko's rule in Belarus and is led by Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, who lives in exile in Lithuania. Her alleged victory over Lukashenko in the disputed 2020 Belarusian presidential election led to national protests. The Wikipedia list places the council among alternative governments in exile of current states.

entries_new.name: United Transitional Cabinet of Belarus
entries_new.mechanism: Opposition figures abroad form a cabinet in waiting.
entries_new.story: The United Transitional Cabinet of Belarus is an opposition body formed in exile in 2022. Belarus has declared it an extremist organisation. It is listed among alternative governments in exile of current states, along with the Coordination Council led by Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya.

entries_new.name: Congress of People's Deputies (Russia, 2022)
entries_new.mechanism: Former deputies abroad claim to be a transitional parliament.
entries_new.story: The Congress of People's Deputies is a meeting of former deputies from different levels and convocations in Russia, claiming to be the transitional parliament of the Russian Federation or its possible successor. Former State Duma deputy Ilya Ponomarev became its public initiator. It is listed among alternative governments in exile of current states, with start year 2022.

entries_new.name: United Liberation Movement for West Papua
entries_new.mechanism: A separatist body abroad campaigns for independence of a territory held by another state.
entries_new.story: The United Liberation Movement for West Papua campaigns for an independent Republic of West Papua and is based in Vanuatu. The Wikipedia list gives 1963 as the start of exile and 1969 for its proclamation, and places it among alternative separatist governments of current subnational territories. Indonesia controls the territory it claims.

entries_new.name: Tatarstan government in exile
entries_new.mechanism: A separatist body abroad claims an independent state for a Russian republic.
entries_new.story: A body listed as the Tatarstan government in exile seeks an independent state of Tatarstan and is based in London. The Wikipedia list gives 1994 as the start and 2008 as its proclamation, and places it among alternative separatist governments of current subnational territories. Russia controls the territory it claims.

entries_new.name: Western Kurdistan Government in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: A separatist body abroad claims a Kurdish state inside Syria.
entries_new.story: The Western Kurdistan Government in Exile aims to found a Kurdish state in Syria and is based in London. The Wikipedia list gives 2004 for its start, and places it among alternative separatist governments of current subnational territories. Syria is the state controlling the territory it claims.

entries_new.name: Kabyle Provisional Government
entries_new.mechanism: A separatist body abroad claims independence for a region of Algeria.
entries_new.story: The Kabyle Provisional Government aims at an independent state of Kabylia, in Algeria, and is based in Paris. The Wikipedia list places its start in 2010 and groups it among alternative separatist governments of current subnational territories. Algeria controls the territory it claims.

entries_new.name: Republican Government of Siena at Montalcino
entries_new.mechanism: Families from a conquered republic set up their own government in a nearby hill town.
entries_new.story: After the city-state of Siena lost the Battle of Marciano and was annexed to the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in 1555, 700 Sienese families refused to accept defeat. They settled in Montalcino and declared themselves the legitimate Republican Government of Siena. The arrangement lasted until 1559, when Tuscan troops arrived at Montalcino.

entries_new.name: Exile government of the Electoral Palatinate
entries_new.mechanism: A dispossessed ruler kept a council in a friendly city to press his claim.
entries_new.story: In the early Thirty Years' War, Maximilian, Elector of Bavaria, occupied the Electoral Palatinate and was awarded it by Emperor Ferdinand II. In late 1622 and early 1623 the fugitive Frederick V, Elector Palatine, organised a Palatinate government in exile at The Hague, headed by Ludwig Camerarius and, from 1627, by Johann Joachim Rusdorf. Frederick died in exile in 1632. The Wikipedia list gives 1648 as the end of the exile government.

entries_new.name: Privy Council of England in exile (Charles II)
entries_new.mechanism: An exiled claimant kept a council in a foreign territory to press his claim.
entries_new.story: During the Interregnum, from 1649 to 1660, the Privy Council of England sat in exile, based for most of the period in the Spanish Netherlands and headed by Charles II. It actively supported his claim to the thrones of England, Scotland and Ireland while the Commonwealth of England ruled at home. The exile ended in 1660.

entries_new.name: Jacobite Privy Council
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed king and his heirs kept a council abroad to maintain their claim.
entries_new.story: After the Glorious Revolution of November 1688, the English Parliament ruled that James II had abandoned the throne, which went to his daughter Mary II and her husband William III. In April 1689 the Scottish Convention did the same. James created a government in exile in France, and his followers became known as Jacobites. After his death in 1701 the claim passed to his son, then to Charles Edward Stuart, who died in 1788. The Wikipedia list gives 1688 to 1788.

entries_new.name: Confederate government of Missouri
entries_new.mechanism: A state government driven out by the war kept operating in another state.
entries_new.story: Missouri had both a Union and a Confederate government during the American Civil War. The Confederate one was driven out of the state and ended up governing from Marshall, Texas. The Wikipedia list gives 1861 to 1865.

entries_new.name: Restored Government of Virginia
entries_new.mechanism: A Unionist state government claimed the state's authority while the Confederacy controlled it.
entries_new.story: The Restored Government of Virginia was the Unionist government of Virginia during the American Civil War, formed in 1861 in opposition to the government that took Virginia into the Confederacy; each regarded the other as illegitimate. It met in Wheeling until that area became part of West Virginia in 1863, then in Alexandria until June 1865, while claiming Richmond as its capital. It never controlled most of the state.

entries_new.name: Hanover exile court and Guelphic Legion
entries_new.challenge: Prussia, then the North German Confederation and the German Empire
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed king kept a court and a small force abroad to preserve his claim.
entries_new.story: On 20 September 1866 Prussia annexed the Kingdom of Hanover. King George V of Hanover lived in exile in Austria, at Hietzing and Gmunden, and never gave up his claim to the throne. From 1866 to 1870 he kept, at his own expense, an exile Hanoverian armed force called the Guelphic Legion. He died in 1878.

entries_new.name: Brazilian Monarchical Directory
entries_new.challenge: Republic of the United States of Brazil
entries_new.mechanism: Monarchists organised a leadership body to work for a restoration.
entries_new.story: The Brazilian Monarchical Directory was the central organisation of the Brazilian monarchist movement, founded in 1890 to coordinate efforts to restore the Empire. It united former imperial statesmen, nobles, intellectuals and regional monarchist branches under one national leadership and acted as the main link with the Imperial Family. The Wikipedia list gives about 1921 as its end.

entries_new.name: Hawaiian royal government in exile
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed monarchy continued to claim authority after a revolution.
entries_new.story: After the Hawaiian Revolution of 1893, the royal government is listed as exiled, with the Republic of Hawaii controlling the territory. The exile ended in 1895, when Queen Liliuokalani abdicated after the Hawaiian Counter-revolution of 1895.

entries_new.name: Belgian government at Sainte-Adresse
entries_new.mechanism: A government displaced by invasion kept operating from allied soil.
entries_new.story: After Germany invaded Belgium in the First World War, the Government of Belgium formed an exile seat at Sainte-Adresse, in France, in 1915. It was disbanded after the restoration of Belgian sovereignty with the Armistice with Germany in 1918.

entries_new.name: Government of the Democratic Republic of Georgia in exile
entries_new.mechanism: The deposed government settled in France after the invasion.
entries_new.story: Formed after the Soviet invasion of Georgia in 1921, the Government of the Democratic Republic of Georgia in exile was based in Leuville-sur-Orge, France. The Wikipedia list gives 1921 to 1954, with the Soviet Union as the state controlling Georgia.

entries_new.name: Government of the Ukrainian People's Republic in exile
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed republic's government continued abroad until Ukraine became independent.
entries_new.story: Formed after the Soviet invasion of Ukraine in 1921, the Government of the Ukrainian People's Republic in exile kept its claim for decades. It was disbanded in 1992, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union. A separate row in the same list records the post of President of Ukraine (in exile), founded on 10 July 1948 and dissolved on 22 August 1992.

entries_new.name: Sublime State of Persia (Qajar exile)
entries_new.mechanism: A deposed dynasty kept its claim to the throne abroad.
entries_new.story: The Qajar dynasty went into exile in 1923 and continued to claim the Iranian throne until the death of Mohammad Hassan Mirza in 1943. The Wikipedia list records this as the Sublime State of Persia, and gives the Imperial State of Iran as the state in control of the territory.

entries_new.name: Generalitat de Catalunya in exile
entries_new.mechanism: A regional government kept a formal existence abroad after its abolition.
entries_new.story: In 1939, as the Spanish Civil War ended with the Republic's defeat, the Francoist dictatorship abolished the Generalitat de Catalunya, the autonomous government of Catalonia, and its president Lluis Companys was tortured and executed. The Generalitat still kept an official existence in exile from 1939 to 1977, when democracy was restored in Spain.

entries_new.name: Estonian governments in exile (Tief and Rei)
entries_new.mechanism: Two rival exile governments claimed to continue the Estonian state.
entries_new.story: After the Soviet annexation of Estonia in 1940, an exile government existed under Otto Tief until January 1953, when it split in two after August Rei removed Tief and a dispute over succession followed. The Rei faction was established in Sweden by members of Tief's government loyal to Rei. It was not recognised by Estonian diplomatic legations that Western countries saw as the legal representatives of the annexed state. The Wikipedia list gives 1991 as the end.

entries_new.name: Latvian and Lithuanian diplomatic services in exile
entries_new.mechanism: Pre-annexation diplomats continued to represent their states abroad.
entries_new.story: After the Soviet annexation of the Baltic states in 1940, the Latvian and Lithuanian diplomatic services continued in exile. The Wikipedia list gives them as running from 1940 to 1991, when the two states regained independence. It lists them as separate rows and does not describe them further.

entries_new.name: Philippine Commonwealth in exile
entries_new.mechanism: A commonwealth government relocated to the allied capital.
entries_new.story: After Japanese forces took control of the Philippines, the Philippine Commonwealth government led by Manuel Quezon fled, first to Melbourne and then to Washington, D.C. It existed in exile from May 1942 to October 1944, when it returned to the Philippines with US forces during the Philippines campaign.

entries_new.name: Emergency Government of the Republic of Indonesia
entries_new.mechanism: A back-up government formed in the interior when the Dutch took the capital.
entries_new.story: The Emergency Government of the Republic of Indonesia was founded after Operatie Kraai, the Dutch military operation of December 1948. Based in Bukittinggi and led by Sjafruddin Prawiranegara, it was disbanded after the Roem-Van Roijen Agreement of 1949.

entries_new.name: All-Palestine Government
entries_new.mechanism: A government proclaimed in Gaza moved to Cairo under Egyptian protection.
entries_new.story: The All-Palestine Government was proclaimed in Gaza in September 1948 and soon relocated to Cairo for fear of an Israeli offensive. Egypt kept control of the Gaza Strip, but the government stayed in exile in Cairo, which gradually stripped it of authority, until it was dissolved in 1959.

entries_new.name: North Korean reserve administration system
entries_new.mechanism: Defectors held titles to administer South Korean divisions in a hypothetical unified state.
entries_new.story: Since the late 1950s North Korea had a government in exile for South Korean administrative divisions, composed of people who had defected from South Korea to the North and were not purged. After their deaths, their children and grandchildren took over. These individuals were meant to take up posts in the South after unification. The Wikipedia list gives 2024 as the end.

entries_new.name: Revolutionary Government of Angola in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: A liberation movement ran a government abroad in a neighbouring country.
entries_new.story: Based in Kinshasa, the Revolutionary Government of Angola in Exile was formed in 1962. Its military branch, the National Liberation Front of Angola, was recognised as a political party in 1992 and holds two seats in Angola's parliament.

entries_new.name: Namibian Government in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: An independence movement held a government abroad.
entries_new.story: Formed by opponents of the apartheid South African administration over South-West Africa, which the United Nations had ruled illegal, the Namibian government in exile was listed from 1966 to 1989. Namibia became independent in 1990 after the South African Border War.

entries_new.name: Crown Council of Ethiopia
entries_new.mechanism: Exiled royalists kept a council to press for restoring the monarchy.
entries_new.story: The Crown Council of Ethiopia formerly opposed the Derg government and sought to restore the Ethiopian monarchy, based in the Washington, D.C., area. On 28 July 2004 it redefined its role, moving from politics to cultural preservation, development and humanitarian work.

entries_new.name: Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea
entries_new.mechanism: An exile coalition with UN recognition opposed the Vietnamese-backed government.
entries_new.story: Established with UN recognition in opposition to the Vietnamese-backed People's Republic of Kampuchea, this coalition government in exile was listed from 1982 to 1993. Elections in 1993 brought the exiled government back into the newly formed Kingdom of Cambodia.

entries_new.name: National Coalition Government of the Union of Burma
entries_new.mechanism: Elected members barred from office formed a government abroad.
entries_new.story: Led by Sein Win and made up of members of parliament elected in 1990 who were not allowed by the military to take office, the National Coalition Government of the Union of Burma was based in Montgomery County, Maryland. It is listed from 1990 to 2012.

entries_new.name: Dubrovnik Republic (1991)
entries_new.mechanism: A short-lived proclamation tied to a former city republic and a federal army.
entries_new.story: Formed in Cavtat, with the help of the Yugoslav People's Army, after Croatia declared independence from Yugoslavia, the Dubrovnik Republic of 1991 claimed to be the historic successor of the Republic of Ragusa (1358 to 1808). The Wikipedia list gives 1991 to 1992 and names Croatia as the controlling state.

entries_new.name: Azerbaijani Community of Nagorno-Karabakh
entries_new.mechanism: Displaced residents organised an association to speak for the region.
entries_new.story: Based in Baku, the Azerbaijani Community of Nagorno-Karabakh was founded on 24 March 1994 and led by Tural Ganjaliyev. The Wikipedia list notes it was not a real government in exile but an association of Azerbaijanis from an area held by Armenian separatists from 1991 to 2020. It announced its dissolution on 30 April 2021 after most of the area returned to Azerbaijani control.

entries_new.name: Kurdish Parliament in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: Kurdish exiles formed a parliament abroad.
entries_new.story: Based in The Hague, the Kurdish Parliament in Exile was founded in April 1995 and led by Yasar Kaya. It was disbanded in 1999. The Wikipedia list names Turkey as the state controlling the territory it claimed.

entries_new.name: Government of Free Vietnam
entries_new.mechanism: Exiles organised themselves as a government in waiting.
entries_new.story: The Government of Free Vietnam was an anti-communist political organisation centred in Garden Grove, California, and Missouri City, Texas. It is listed from 1995 and was disbanded in 2013. The state controlling the territory it claimed was the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

entries_new.name: Bongo Doit Partir
entries_new.mechanism: An exile movement presented itself as an alternative government.
entries_new.story: Bongo Doit Partir, French for Bongo Must Go, was founded by Daniel Mengara in opposition to Gabonese president Omar Bongo. After Bongo's death in June 2009, Mengara returned to Gabon to take part in the country's elections. The Wikipedia list gives 1998 to 2009.

entries_new.name: Quetta Shura
entries_new.mechanism: Leaders of a toppled government regrouped across the border in Pakistan.
entries_new.story: After the Taliban were removed from power in the 2001 Afghan war, veteran leaders of the former government, including Mullah Mohammed Omar, the Taliban's founder and spiritual leader, fled to Quetta in Balochistan Province, Pakistan. The Wikipedia list describes the Quetta Shura as a continuation of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, and gives 2001 to 2021.

entries_new.name: Royal Lao Government in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: Exiles proclaimed a royal government abroad.
entries_new.story: Based in Gresham, Oregon, the Royal Lao Government in Exile opposed the communist government of Laos and sought a constitutional monarchy. It is listed from 2003 until its self-proclaimed prime minister died, with 2023 as the end date (marked in the source as needing a citation).

entries_new.name: Interim Government of Federated Shan States
entries_new.mechanism: Shan leaders proclaimed an interim government for independence.
entries_new.story: The Interim Government of the Federated Shan States aimed to establish an independent state for the Shan ethnic group in Myanmar. The Wikipedia list gives 2005 to 2006 and notes it became defunct within several months.

entries_new.name: Provisional Administration of South Ossetia
entries_new.mechanism: A provincial administration continued in the capital after losing control of its territory.
entries_new.story: A Georgian provincial administration led by Tamaz Bestayev, the Provisional Administration of South Ossetia was based in Tbilisi. After the 2008 South Ossetia war it had no South Ossetian territory under its control and remained a nominal body until it was abolished on 31 December 2025, per the Wikipedia list's 2025 end date.

entries_new.name: Syrian Interim Government
entries_new.mechanism: An opposition body governed some areas from within the country.
entries_new.story: The Syrian Interim Government opposed Ba'athist Syria and had ties to some Free Syrian Army groups; it was based in Azaz. After the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, it coexisted for a short time with the caretaker government headed by Mohammed al-Bashir in Damascus. The Wikipedia list gives 2013 to 2025.

entries_new.name: New Zaire Government in Exile
entries_new.mechanism: An opposition politician abroad declared a government for the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
entries_new.story: The New Zaire Government in Exile was established in Brussels in May 2017 by Congolese opposition politician Christian Malanga of the United Congolese Party. Malanga was killed during an unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the Congolese government on 19 May 2024. The Wikipedia list gives 2017 to 2024.

entries_new.name: Montenegrin State Council (Zagreb)
entries_new.stopped_by: Fall of the Independent State of Croatia, 1945
entries_new.mechanism: An Axis-aligned leader formed an exile government in an allied capital.
entries_new.story: After the Germans withdrew from Montenegro in 1944, the fascist leader Sekula Drljevic founded a government in exile based in Zagreb, capital of the Independent State of Croatia. He also set up the Montenegrin National Army, a force formed with Croatian fascist leader Ante Pavelic. The government was dissolved after the fall of the Independent State of Croatia, with the Wikipedia list giving 8 May 1945.

entries_new.name: Legionary Romania (government in exile in Vienna)
entries_new.mechanism: Germany set up an exile government after Romania changed sides.
entries_new.story: Germany had imprisoned Horia Sima and other Iron Guard members after the Legionnaires' rebellion of 1941. After King Michael's Coup in 1944 brought a pro-Allied government to power in Romania, Germany released Sima to establish a pro-Axis government in exile in Vienna. It raised a Romanian National Army in the SS of 12,000 men that fought alongside Germany until the end of the war. The list gives 8 May 1945 as its end.

entries_new.name: Sigmaringen Governmental Commission
entries_new.challenge: Provisional Government of the French Republic
entries_new.mechanism: Germany installed a displaced French government in a town it controlled.
entries_new.story: Members of the collaborationist French cabinet of Vichy were relocated by the Germans to the enclave of Sigmaringen in Germany, where they formed a government in exile until April 1945. They were given formal governmental power over the city, and Germany, Italy and Japan opened what were officially their embassies to France there. Philippe Petain refused to take part, so the commission was headed by Fernand de Brinon.

entries_new.name: Bulgarian government in exile (Tsankov)
entries_new.mechanism: Opponents of the new Bulgarian government set up an exile government in German-held territory.
entries_new.story: Formed after the 1944 Bulgarian coup brought socialists to power in Bulgaria, this government in exile was based in Vienna and headed by Aleksandar Tsankov. It raised the 1st Bulgarian Regiment of the SS. The Wikipedia list gives 16 September 1944 to 10 May 1945.

entries_new.name: Hellenic State in exile (Vienna)
entries_new.stopped_by: Capture during the Vienna offensive, April 1945
entries_new.mechanism: Collaborationist ministers regrouped in Vienna after Greece was liberated.
entries_new.story: After the liberation of Greece, former collaborationist ministers set up a new government in Vienna in September 1944. It was headed by Ektor Tsironikos, a former collaborationist minister. In April 1945, Tsironikos and his ministers were captured during the Vienna offensive.

entries_new.name: Hungarian Government of National Unity (Szalasi)
entries_new.mechanism: A government retreating from the Red Army re-formed in German territory.
entries_new.story: As the Soviet advance went through Hungary, the Szalasi government fled on 28 and 29 March 1945. It was first based in Vienna and then in Munich. Most of its leaders were arrested in the months after the Allied victory in Europe, in which the list gives 7 May 1945 as the end.

entries_new.name: Slovak Republic government in exile (Kremsmunster)
entries_new.mechanism: A wartime government retreated to Austrian territory as Soviet forces advanced.
entries_new.story: The government of the Slovak Republic, led by Jozef Tiso, went into exile on 4 April 1945 to the Austrian town of Kremsmunster as the Red Army took Bratislava and occupied Slovakia. The exiled government capitulated to the American general Walton Walker on 8 May 1945.

entries_new.name: Second Philippine Republic in exile
entries_new.mechanism: The wartime government continued in name outside the Philippines.
entries_new.story: After Allied forces liberated the Philippines and the Philippine Commonwealth was re-established there, the Second Philippine Republic became a nominal government in exile. The Wikipedia list gives 11 June 1945 to 17 August 1945. It was the Japanese-aligned government of the Philippines of 1943 to 1945.

entries_new.name: Croatian government in exile (Argentina)
entries_new.mechanism: Former officials of a wartime state set up a government abroad.
entries_new.story: Many former members of the government of the Independent State of Croatia fled to Argentina. From there they founded a government in exile on 10 April 1951, and the Wikipedia list gives 28 December 1959 as its end. The state controlling the claimed territory was Yugoslavia.

entries_new.name: Greek Cypriot municipal councils in exile (Lapithos, Kythrea)
entries_new.mechanism: Displaced town officials keep municipal councils running in the capital.
entries_new.story: After the Turkish invasion of Cyprus in 1974 and the displacement of many Greek Cypriots from the north, displaced residents of several towns set up what are in effect municipal councils in exile, headed by mayors in exile. The aim is to assert a continuing legitimate rule and work toward restoring control. The Municipal Council of Lapithos met in members' homes, then in offices at 37 Ammochostou Street, Nicosia, shared with the Exile Municipal Council of Kythrea.

entries_new.name: Company of the American Islands
entries_new.founder: Cardinal Richelieu charged Francois Fouquet with reviving it
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave a company the right to settle and govern French Caribbean islands.
entries_new.story: The Company of the American Islands was a French chartered company that in 1635 took over the administration of the French part of Saint-Christophe (Saint Kitts) and was charged with settling other Caribbean islands and converting their inhabitants to Catholicism. Under its direction France settled Guadeloupe and Martinique (1635), St Lucia (1643), St Martin and St Barts (1648), Grenada (1649) and St Croix (1650). The company received a twenty-year charter extension in 1642 but languished, and in 1651 it dissolved itself and sold its rights; the du Parquet family bought Martinique, Grenada and Saint Lucia for 60,000 livres.

entries_new.name: French West India Company
entries_new.mechanism: A state-funded charter gave one company the French colonies in America and trading posts in Africa.
entries_new.story: The French West India Company was a trading company of the Kingdom of France, founded in May 1664 on the plan of Louis XIV's minister Colbert and closed in late 1674, after the Franco-Dutch War. The king subscribed two million livres against 1.3 million from private investors. Its grant covered French America and trading posts on the African coast from Cape Verde to the Cape of Good Hope. In 1665 it obtained the Carignan-Salieres regiment for New France, and in 1666 it opened trading posts at Savi and Ouidah in Dahomey.
entries_new.anchor: New France and the French Caribbean

entries_new.name: Swedish South Company (New Sweden)
entries_new.stopped_by: New Netherland annexed New Sweden in 1655
entries_new.mechanism: A chartered trading company supported a colony on the Delaware River.
entries_new.story: The Swedish South Company, also called the Company of New Sweden, was a Swedish trading company founded in 1626 to support trade between Sweden and its colony New Sweden in North America. The colony was envisioned by Willem Usselincx as the first Swedish overseas trading project. The company lost its tobacco monopoly, granted by the queen in 1641, in 1649. New Sweden was annexed by New Netherland in 1655, which ended the company's activities, and it was dissolved in 1680.

entries_new.name: Royal African Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal charter gave one company a monopoly on English trade with Africa.
entries_new.story: The Royal African Company was an English trading company established in 1660 by the House of Stuart and City of London merchants to trade along the West African coast, with a monopoly on English trade with Africa overseen by the Duke of York. It began with gold in the Gambia River and quickly turned to the slave trade, shipping about 100,000 enslaved Africans to the Americas. Parliament pressed William III to end the monopoly in 1697, the company was insolvent by 1708, and its assets passed in 1752 to the African Company of Merchants.

entries_new.name: Brandenburg African Company
entries_new.mechanism: An electoral charter let a company run fortified posts on the Guinea coast.
entries_new.story: The Brandenburg African Company was chartered by Frederick William, Elector of Brandenburg, in May 1682 and ran a small colony of two Gold Coast settlements near Cape Three Points in present-day Ghana, with Gross Friedrichsburg as capital. The colony became the Prussian Gold Coast in 1701 and was abandoned in 1717. In 1721 Prussia sold it to the Dutch West India Company for 7,200 ducats and 12 enslaved boys in gold chains. The source says its trade centred on enslaved people, and that Prussia also leased part of St Thomas from Denmark.

entries_new.name: Ostend Company
entries_new.mechanism: An imperial charter gave an Austrian-Netherlands company trading posts in India.
entries_new.story: The Ostend Company was a chartered trading company in the Austrian Netherlands, chartered by the Austrian ruler Charles VI in December 1722 to trade with the East and West Indies. It had 6 million guilders in capital and two trading posts, at Covelong on the Coromandel Coast and at Banquibazar (Ichapore) in Bengal. It competed strongly in the tea trade with China. After British diplomatic pressure on Austria, it was ordered to close in 1731, a condition for the Treaty of Vienna and an alliance between the two states.

entries_new.name: Swedish West India Company
entries_new.mechanism: A royal monopoly on trade through a Swedish island was given to a private firm.
entries_new.story: The Swedish West India Company was a Swedish chartered company based in the West Indies and the main operator of the Swedish slave trade while it existed. From 1786 to 1805 it operated from the Swedish island of Saint-Barthelemy as a private enterprise with a royal monopoly on all Swedish trade via the island. Three quarters of profits went to the company and one quarter to the Swedish state.
